column1: # T7 (Ludmil, 28 Sep): "freeze and record versions/checksums of KrakenUniq/Bracken, GTDB,
# CheckM2, geNomad, MLST and any other DB".
# The reference databases this pipeline reads, frozen as of frozen_on. Written and read by
# scripts/record_database_versions.sh: every run recomputes `fingerprint` for the databases
# it was actually pointed at and compares it with this file, and RUN_REPORT.txt's DATABASES
# section prints the release, the fingerprint and whether it matched (frozen / CHANGED /
# not_in_manifest). A run against a rebuilt or substituted database is then visible in the
# run's own record, instead of being indistinguishable from the validated runs because the
# path string happened not to change. Checked by tests/test_database_versions.py.
# FINGERPRINT METHODS
#   sha256:listing   sha256 over a sorted listing of "<relative path>\t<size in bytes>" for
#                    every regular file in the tree (one line, for a single file). This is
#                    what is recomputed on every run. It is used because these databases are
#                    far too large to checksum per run -- KrakenUniq's database.kdb alone is
#                    574 GB and the whole set is 706 GB, which is tens of minutes of pure
#                    read against shared Lustre, every run, to learn nothing new. The
#                    listing is O(file count): the full set above takes under a second. It
#                    changes whenever a database is rebuilt, re-downloaded or extended. It
#                    does NOT catch an in-place edit that preserves every file's size.
#   sha256:content   sha256 of the file itself. Recomputed per run only for files at or
#                    below PKS_DB_HASH_MAX_BYTES (default 2 GiB); none of these qualify.
# key_file / key_file_sha256 is the backstop for what the listing cannot see: a real
# content sha256 of one small, release-defining file per database, computed once when the
# database was frozen. It is NOT recomputed per run -- verifying it is a deliberate act:
#     sha256sum <path>/<key_file>
# and the answer must equal key_file_sha256 below.
# Sizes and file counts are as measured on TSCC on frozen_on. `release` is read from the
# marker the database itself ships (GTDB-Tk metadata/metadata.txt VERSION_DATA, geNomad
# version.txt, CheckM2 CONTENTS.json "version"), never inferred from the directory name --
# a directory can be renamed, or a newer release dropped into the old name, which is
# exactly the failure this file exists to catch.
# NOT listed as rows, because they have no path parameter to fingerprint:
#   Bracken   has no database of its own. Its read-length models are the
#             database<N>mers.kmer_distrib files INSIDE the KrakenUniq directory below, so
#             they are already covered by the kraken_db row; --bracken_read_length selects
#             which one. Bracken's own version is pinned in conda_envs/krakenUniq_bracken_env.yml.
#   MLST      the PubMLST scheme snapshot ships inside the conda package and is frozen by
#             the pin mlst=2.35.0 in conda_envs/mlst_env.yml, with blast=2.16.0 (the tool
#             that does the calling) pinned alongside it. There is no --mlst_db parameter,
#             so there is nothing on disk here to fingerprint.
# name
kraken_db
